Russia has emerged as a preferred destination for Indian students aspiring to study MBBS. When choosing between private medical colleges in Nepal and India, factors such as budget and future career plans play an important role. Nepal generally offers a more affordable and predictable fee structure, with total costs ranging from ₹60-70 lakh, along with NEET-based admissions and relatively lower competition. In India, fees vary significantly depending on the type of seat, ranging from around ₹45–60 lakh under state quota to over ₹1 crore for management quota seats. Both countries provide English-medium education and degrees recognized by the National Medical Commission (NMC). However, students graduating from Nepal must qualify FMGE/NExT to practice medicine in India. Before applying, it is essential to confirm the recognition and accreditation status of the medical college.

The National Testing Agency released the NEET UG 2026 Re-Exam Provisional Answer Key on June 25. Candidates can raise objections until June 28 by paying ₹200 per question. The fee will be fully refunded if the challenge is found to be valid. Make sure to submit objections using your own question paper series code and attach supporting evidence. The expert review process will take place alongside OMR evaluation to speed up the declaration of results. Visit the official NTA portal and complete the process before the deadline.

Georgia is becoming an increasingly popular choice for international students who want a quality European education at an affordable cost. With low tuition fees, affordable living expenses, and good career opportunities after graduation, the country offers several benefits for students. For those planning to study in Georgia, having a clear understanding of the student visa process is an important step.

The CSCA exam has become a mandatory requirement for Indian PCB students seeking admission to MBBS programs in China. The exam evaluates candidates in Mathematics and Chemistry, with Mathematics often being the most difficult section for students without a math background. It is conducted online from home using a dual-camera monitoring system. However, qualifying the CSCA exam alone does not ensure eligibility to practice medicine in India. Students must also meet NMC regulations, achieve HSK Level 4 proficiency in Mandarin, and pass the CMQE licensing examination. Early preparation and planning are strongly recommended.

For NEET 2025, Tamil Nadu remained the most competitive state in South India for MBBS admissions. CMC Vellore recorded an impressive AIR 37 under the AIQ. Top government colleges required around 715–725 marks for General category candidates. Despite offering nearly 11,700 MBBS seats, including 350 newly added seats, demand continued to exceed availability. Tamil Nadu's cutoff levels remained higher than those in Kerala and Karnataka. State quota admissions are conducted by DME Tamil Nadu. Candidates should prepare and plan their counselling choices carefully.

For NEET UG 2026, the expected cutoff for government medical colleges is: qualifying marks 135-145 (General), but admission-safe scores are much higher - General 620-650+ for AIQ, 570-620+ for State Quota. State-wise cutoffs vary, with Chandigarh expected around 650 and Assam around 540. Category-wise safe scores are estimated at: OBC 590-615+, SC 520-550+, and ST 480-520+. Plan your counselling choices accordingly.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has proposed extending the maximum duration to complete the MBBS course, including the compulsory internship, from 9 years to 10 years under the GMER Amendment 2026. The existing rule allowing only four attempts to clear the First Professional MBBS examination remains unchanged. The draft regulations are currently open for public comments until June 27, 2026. If approved, the revision could provide additional flexibility for students whose studies are delayed due to health issues, academic setbacks, or other unforeseen circumstances.

Choosing between a deemed medical college and pursuing MBBS in Europe mainly depends on your budget and long-term career plans. Deemed colleges in India can cost up to ₹1.5 crore, but they provide strong clinical exposure in India and make PG preparation easier. On the other hand, MBBS in Europe is more affordable, but students must meet strict NMC guidelines, including 54 months of study, a 12-month internship in the same country, English-medium education, and clearing FMGE/NExT. If you aim for an international career, Europe can be a better option, while deemed colleges are more suitable for students planning to practice in India.

Applying for a China visa? Don’t let a simple photo mistake delay your plans. Your visa photo must meet strict guidelines to ensure smooth processing.

The required China visa photo size is 33mm x 48mm, with your face covering 70–80% of the frame. Your head height should be between 28mm and 33mm, properly centered and clearly visible. Make sure the photo is taken within the last 6 months and reflects your current appearance without any edits or filters.

Keep a neutral expression while looking straight at the camera. Avoid smiling, tilting your head, or wearing glasses and non-religious headwear. The background must be plain white, free from shadows, patterns, or any distractions.

Following these China visa photo requirements carefully can help you avoid rejections and ensure a faster, hassle-free visa process.

They may be good with specific UK and Ireland universities, maybe a few in the US (probably the ones that have a high acceptance rate). But if your aim is to apply to some top high ranking universities, I am sorry but Global Opportunities would be the worst choice.

My review is localised to the Dadar branch based on my experience. I hope branches in some other states would be somewhat credible. GO dadar is not.
